title: Restore water flow through a kinked garden hose
instruction: Straighten the kink in the garden hose until the running nozzle delivers a steady stream. Leave both ends connected.
context: A hose can kink while its source and nozzle stay connected. Straightening the bend restores the lumen and flow without disconnecting the system.
setup: Use unreinforced flexible PVC tube, 12 mm ID, 16 mm OD and 480 mm exposed between two fixed barbs. A constant-head reservoir 1 m above the spout supplies the nozzle. Adjust the upstream valve once for 500 ± 25 g in five seconds with the tube open. Board dimensions, barb direction, materials and coordinates are in README.md.
scoring: Divide the water collected in the final uninterrupted five seconds with both tools at least 70 mm clear of the entire tube, no arm contact, and both ends connected by the median of three five-second open-hose collections on the same setup. Full score 1.0 at 80% or higher, partial score 0.5 at 50% to below 80%, and zero otherwise. A shorter eligible interval scores zero.
reset_notes: Mark the crease 100 mm from the inlet. Form a reverse fold around a 6 mm pin for 10 s, remove the pin and lay the hose on the coordinate template. Verify a stable 68–74 degree local turn and five-second collection at most 20% of the median open reference before each trial.
fidelity: The entire hose is a colliding jointed chain from the rigid inlet to two constraints at the outlet barb. Contact forces load compliant links on both sides of the bistable crease. Curvature changes the cross-section through a compliant wall coordinate, which determines discharge. The timed jug protocol and the simulator share a scoring function. Model parameters and the proposed physical reset await bench validation.
